name: GA-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Scott holds an overwhelming cash advantage over a barely funded challenger
Prediction markets price the seat near 98 percent Republican
No polls or expert ratings show the race in play
model.rationale: A fifteen-point Republican lean, Austin Scott's incumbency, and a roughly fifty-to-one gap in cash on hand leave Kelly Esti without a visible path; the margin settles a bit beyond the district lean because the challenger's campaign shows almost no measurable activity.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending on Esti's behalf or a sharp national shift against Republicans could narrow the margin, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Austin Scott enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a district that leans Republican by fifteen points. He reports about $1.4 million raised and the same amount on hand, while Democrat Kelly Esti has raised under $30,000 with less than $4,000 available. No public polls cover the race and no expert raters list it as competitive, but prediction markets give Scott roughly a 98 percent chance of holding the seat.

Every measurable factor points the same way: the district's partisan lean, the power of incumbency, and a lopsided money gap all favor Scott, and the challenger's campaign shows little visible activity. Expect Scott to win by roughly seventeen or eighteen points, with the genuine uncertainty limited to the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
